summary: Iter 10 full backend + frontend regression. Added 31 pytest cases covering /api/users/me (service_view), /api/equipment CRUD + status computation for engine/lifting/bop_pce/reel_iron, log actions (service/test/inspection/hours_update/meters_update/pressure_update), /api/schedule with one_off + 14/14 + custom rotation expansion (verified 2 cycles produce 2 shifts starting 2026-02-16 & 2026-03-16), invalid-input 400s, list/patch/delete, plus regression on /auth/me, /manager/dashboard, /crew/handover-summary, /team/items. Frontend: Hub NEW badges + navigation, /equipment page create engine 225h → AMBER pill → log service → OK pill → delete, /schedule page open + 14/14 pattern save (backend accepted 2 shifts, cleaned up via API), Service Toggle on /app hides Sand_Cleanout & CT_Milling, keeps Annular_Frac + Frac_Through_CT, localStorage='stand_alone_frac' persists across reload. All 31/31 backend tests pass; all frontend flows pass.

issues: Three NEW badges (Equipment, Schedule, Training Mode) — matches code but if only Equipment + Schedule were intended to be flagged NEW this iter, consider dropping the Training badge.

14-day grid is anchored at today; shifts created for a date range outside the current window are silently invisible until user navigates via schedule-prev/next. Consider auto-anchoring to the earliest new shift after save, or a toast confirming shift creation with a jump link.

critical_code_review_comments: server.py is now 1957 lines — approaching maintainability threshold. Consider splitting equipment + schedule modules into their own routers (backend/routes/equipment.py, backend/routes/schedule.py).
/api/schedule GET builds a `window` dict with unused keys ('end_date_lte') before overwriting query with `cond` — the `window` local is dead code; safe to remove.

Equipment list rig-filter uses `$or: [{rig_id: rig_id}, {rig_id: None}, {rig_id: {'$exists': False}}]` which will return legacy untagged items alongside the requested rig. That's intentional (matches team_items pattern) but users viewing Rig 2 see equipment that was never assigned — worth documenting.
ScheduleShiftCreate.rotation_days_on/off ignored for non-custom patterns is fine, but _pattern_to_on_off is called 3× per doc during insert (line 1891/1892) — negligible cost but redundant.
PATCH /users/me: on success returns raw user doc but includes potentially large embedded fields (subscription_status, trial_expires_at) — ok, just note it's an implicit /auth/me subset.

EquipmentPage KindFields uses `equip-${kind}-${k}` for both text/date/num inputs — duplicates data-testid on `serial_number` (declared both at line 376 and possibly reused). No collision observed but worth auditing.
CrewSchedule 14-day grid does not auto-scroll to the newly-created shift's start date, causing 'shifts saved but nothing shown' UX confusion (see design_issues).
seed_data_creation: All test rows prefixed TEST_ / UITEST_ and cleaned up via DELETE in fixtures & JS eval. No residual data left in team_dcb3ba5cfed0.
context_for_next_testing_agent: iter10 backend suite is at /app/backend/tests/test_iter10_equipment_schedule.py — safe to re-run with `pytest backend/tests/test_iter10_equipment_schedule.py -n 0`. Uses env REACT_APP_BACKEND_URL (falls back to /app/frontend/.env). All computed-status inputs are date-relative to _today()_ so the amber/red thresholds keep working over time. Frontend Advisory modal blocks pointer events on first paint — dismiss it before every hub/app interaction. Schedule grid is anchored to today (14-day window); shifts far in the future won't render until schedule-prev/next navigation.
